Nel carcinoma gastrico la TC serve a ved:
In gastric carcinoma, CT is used to show the site and extent of the tumor and above all to look for metastases (liver, peritoneum, distant lymph nodes). The wall is best assessed with the stomach distended by water or gas: a normal distended wall measures a few millimeters; a wall over 1 cm, irregular or with focal mucosal enhancement is suspicious.
Pitfalls: a contracted antrum can look thickened (compare the phases and look for preserved layering); diffuse tumor may cause only rigid thickening without a mass; CT underestimates lymph nodes (metastases in small nodes) and peritoneal carcinomatosis, which is why staging laparoscopy is performed in locally advanced tumors.
Signs of T4a: irregular serosal contour, stranding or nodules in the perigastric fat; T4b: invasion of the pancreas, transverse colon, liver, spleen.
Differential diagnosis of gastric wall thickening: gastritis and ulcer (mild thickening, preserved layering), lymphoma (very marked thickening, often with bulky nodes and without obstruction), GIST (exophytic submucosal mass).
Ispessimento irregolare della parete gas: Irregular gastric wall thickening that persists in all phases: tumor until proven otherwise; CT underestimates lymph nodes and peritoneum.
